sentences.text: Subhas Chandra Bose -LRB- 23 January 1897 -- 18 August 1945 -RRB- was an Indian nationalist whose defiant patriotism made him a hero in India , but whose attempt during World War II to rid India of British rule with the help of Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan left a troubled legacy .	Indian nationalist	Indian independence movement	World War II	World War II	British rule	British Raj	Nazi Germany	Nazi Germany	Imperial Japan	Imperial Japan

The honorific Netaji -LRB- Hindustani : `` Respected Leader '' -RRB- , first applied in early 1942 to Bose in Germany by the Indian soldiers of the Indische Legion and by the German and Indian officials in the Special Bureau for India in Berlin , was later used throughout India .	Hindustani	Hindustani language	Indische Legion	Indische Legion	Special Bureau for India	Special Bureau for India	Berlin	Berlin

Bose had been a leader of the younger , radical , wing of the Indian National Congress in the late 1920s and 1930s , rising to become Congress President in 1938 and 1939 .	Indian National Congress	Indian National Congress
However , he was ousted from Congress leadership positions in 1939 following differences with Mahatma Gandhi and the Congress high command .	Mahatma Gandhi	Mahatma Gandhi
He was subsequently placed under house arrest by the British before escaping from India in 1940 .

Bose arrived in Germany in April 1941 , where the leadership offered unexpected , if sometimes ambivalent , sympathy for the cause of India 's independence , contrasting starkly with its attitudes towards other colonised peoples and ethnic communities .
In November 1941 , with German funds , a Free India Centre was set up in Berlin , and soon a Free India Radio , on which Bose broadcast nightly .	Berlin	Berlin

A 3,000-strong Free India Legion , comprising Indians captured by Erwin Rommel 's Afrika Korps , was also formed to aid in a possible future German land invasion of India .	Free India Legion	Free India Legion	Erwin Rommel	Erwin Rommel	Afrika Korps	Afrika Korps
By spring 1942 , in light of Japanese victories in southeast Asia and changing German priorities , a German invasion of India became untenable , and Bose became keen to move to southeast Asia .
Adolf Hitler , during his only meeting with Bose in late May 1942 , suggested the same , and offered to arrange for a submarine .	Adolf Hitler	Adolf Hitler

During this time Bose also became a father ; his wife , or companion , Emilie Schenkl , whom he had met in 1934 , gave birth to a baby girl in November 1942 .	Emilie Schenkl	Emilie Schenkl	a baby girl	Anita Bose Pfaff
Identifying strongly with the Axis powers , and no longer apologetically , Bose boarded a German submarine in February 1943 .	Axis powers	Axis powers
In Madagascar , he was transferred to a Japanese submarine from which he disembarked in Japanese-held Sumatra in May 1943 .	Japanese-held	Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies	Sumatra	Sumatra

With Japanese support , Bose revamped the Indian National Army -LRB- INA -RRB- , then composed of Indian soldiers of the British Indian army who had been captured in the Battle of Singapore .	Indian National Army	Indian National Army	Battle of Singapore	Battle of Singapore
To these , after Bose 's arrival , were added enlisting Indian civilians in Malaya and Singapore .

The Japanese had come to support a number of puppet and provisional governments in the captured regions , such as those in Burma , the Philippines and Manchukuo .	Burma	Japanese occupation of Burma	Philippines	Second Philippine Republic	Manchukuo	Manchukuo

Before long the Provisional Government of Free India , presided by Bose , was formed in the Japanese-occupied Andaman and Nicobar Islands .	Provisional Government of Free India	Azad Hind	Andaman and Nicobar Islands	Andaman and Nicobar Islands

Bose had great drive and charisma -- creating popular Indian slogans , such as `` Jai Hind , '' -- and the INA under Bose was a model of diversity by region , ethnicity , religion , and even gender .	Jai Hind	Jai Hind
However , Bose was regarded by the Japanese as being militarily unskilled , and his military effort was short-lived .
In late 1944 and early 1945 the British Indian Army first halted and then devastatingly reversed the Japanese attack on India .	British Indian Army	British Indian Army	attack on India	Operation U-Go
Almost half the Japanese forces and fully half the participating INA contingent were killed .
The INA was driven down the Malay Peninsula , and surrendered with the recapture of Singapore .	recapture of Singapore	Operation Tiderace

Bose had earlier chosen not to surrender with his forces or with the Japanese , but rather to escape to Manchuria with a view to seeking a future in the Soviet Union which he believed to be turning anti-British .
He died from third degree burns received when his plane crashed in Taiwan .
Some Indians , however , did not believe that the crash had occurred , with many among them , especially in Bengal , believing that Bose would return to gain India 's independence .

Indian National Congress , the main instrument of Indian nationalism , praised Bose 's patriotism but distanced itself from his tactics and ideology , especially his collaboration with Fascism .	Indian National Congress	Indian National Congress

The British Raj , though never seriously threatened by the INA , charged 300 INA officers with treason in the INA trials , but eventually backtracked in the face both of popular sentiment and of its own end .	British Raj	British Raj	INA trials	INA trials
